newsitem.title: UK: European home online market set for rapid growth.
newsitem.headline: European home online market set for rapid growth.

text.p: The European market for domestic online services will grow nine-fold over the next five years, a report released on Friday forecast.
European consumer online revenues are set to increase from $1.5 billion to $13.7 billion between 1997 and 2001, said the report issued by strategic management consultants Datamonitor.
The report estimated that online subscription revenues would rise from $1.3 billion in 1997 to almost $9.1 billion in 2001.
The Internet shopping market is expected to rise from $75 million in the current year to $3.3 billion, while revenue from online games is set to grow from $135 million to $1.3 billion.
Multiplayer online games were identified as a key selling point for online services in general.

The report noted that the online shopping market in 2001 would remain small in comparison with the mail order market. But it said that European online shoppers would not be traditional users of home shopping, who tend to come from lower income groups, but more affluent computer users.
The study also noted huge differences between European countries in the amounts charged for Internet and online use. The lowest chares were reported in Italy and the highest in Austria.

It said the level of competition and the socio-economic situation in individual countries were factors behind the differing rates. Tax levels and the cost of employment were also important elements in fixing charges.
